items.headline: Zscaler ships the first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI, covering MCP channels, non-human identities, and endpoint AI threats
items.diff_narrative: A new AI-security infrastructure storyline opens with no counterpart yesterday. At its Zenith Live 2026 conference Zscaler announced three products — AI Broker (inline MCP/A2A enforcement with an Agent Registry), AI Access Graph (identity-and-data-lineage from the $175M Symmetry Systems acquisition), and Endpoint AI Security (browser extensions, plugins, and local AI tools) — which together it positions as the industry's first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI. An Oasis Security integration announced June 10 adds lifecycle governance for non-human identities on top of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange. Neither the Zscaler platform nor the Oasis integration appeared in yesterday's report.

items.headline: Databricks Data + AI Summit: Agent Bricks and OpenSharing formalize agentic infrastructure on Day 2
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's Databricks coverage centered on the Omnigent meta-harness, a standalone Apache-2.0 project wrapping Claude Code, Codex, and agent SDKs behind a common interface. Today that thread advances to the summit's Day 2 main announcements. Agent Bricks — a three-pillar (Choice, Context, Control) developer platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents in production — is the headline launch, with over 100,000 agents already built on the underlying infrastructure processing more than one quadrillion tokens annually; it integrates LangGraph, Agno, CrewAI, Claude Code SDK, MCP with Unity Catalog, a Genie Ontology layer, agent-memory via Lakebase, and a Databricks Sandbox. OpenSharing, a vendor-neutral Linux Foundation protocol extending Delta Sharing to agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data with founding partners including OpenAI, SAP, Stripe, Atlassian, and Amadeus, is announced alongside it. Omnigent is not featured in today's report.

items.headline: SGLang v0.5.13 ships Nemotron 3 Ultra and Cosmos 3 support with production-ready speculative decoding
items.diff_narrative: A new inference-engine release lands with no counterpart yesterday. SGLang v0.5.13, released June 13, adds model support for Nemotron 3 Ultra, Step-3.7-Flash, Command A+, and diffusion models including Cosmos 3 and FLUX.2-Klein, promotes Spec V2 tree drafting with topk greater than 1 to production-ready status across triton, FA3, MLA, and aiter backends, extends piecewise CUDA Graph coverage to DSA models and DeepSeek V4, and adds real-time video generation for SGLang-Diffusion. The local-model slot yesterday was occupied by the CacheRL research paper on cached-rollout RL for small tool-calling agents; that paper is absent today.

items.headline: Anthropic Fable 5 export ban: senior technical staff dispatched to Washington in fast-moving negotiation
items.diff_narrative: The Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspension story advances with new developments. The situation escalated on June 15 as Anthropic sent senior technical staff to Washington to pursue a negotiated resolution with the administration, which issued the June 12 directive after citing a jailbreak technique involving asking the model to read a codebase and fix software flaws. As of June 16, both models remain offline globally while Anthropic negotiates; a live resolution is moving unusually fast for Washington, with some officials signaling openness to a technical compromise. Security researcher Katie Moussouris and others have publicly noted that the cited capability is standard defensive security work and is present in competing systems including GPT-5.5.

items.headline: AI events calendar: Data + AI Summit continues through Wednesday as Bay Area schedule fills before AI Engineer World's Fair
items.diff_narrative: The three-track calendar (mainstream dev/data, AI-security, AI-chip) continues with the same anchor events but several new entries and status shifts. The Data + AI Summit is now mid-run (through June 18) rather than opening-day. New additions for AI-security: an AICamp invite-only AI Agent Security Documentary Premiere tonight (June 16, 6-9 PM PDT, 582 Market St, San Francisco) with former White House CIO Theresa Payton and MIT's Ramesh Raskar; an AI Tinkerers Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25; and the SecurityWeek AI Risk Summit (August 11-12, Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay) which was not listed yesterday. Snowflake Dev Day (June 25, San Francisco) appears for the first time. The Confidential Computing Summit, AMD Advancing AI, Hot Chips, AI Infra Summit, AI Engineer World's Fair, Black Hat/DEF CON, OWASP AppSec, GitHub Universe, and AWS re:Invent all carry forward.
